issue_plan.name: Codex on chosen projects
issue_plan.summary: Eight plumbing issues let a project choose Codex or Claude Code, and run Codex under the same rules, limits, view and records as Claude Code, as D-0028 and D-0052 planned; running both on one issue, and hosted runs, stay out. First comes the choice: an issue's Agent: line, its project's manifest and the watcher's -agent, with Claude Code the default, and every record naming its agent. Then the factory takes back only regular files from an agent's workspace, gains a Codex backend, and runs Codex only where it can see nothing but its workspace. How it does that is @gitdek's decision, which that issue asks as a fork before any of it is built. Last, the watcher checks its agents at start, the live view shows Codex's runs, and the docs say how a person gives Codex the decision graph's tools.

issues.title: Let each issue and project choose its coding agent
issues.body:
@gitdek wants some projects built with Codex and the rest with Claude Code (#153). The factory runs every agent through `synth.Backend`, whose only implementation is Claude Code (D-0028, D-0052). This issue makes the agent a choice, as the language is (D-0040). Codex comes in later issues, so for now Claude Code stays the only agent the factory can run.

- An issue picks its agent with a line of its own, `Agent: codex` or `Agent: claude-code`, read as the factory reads an issue's Project: line: outside code blocks, the first one counting.
- When the factory creates a project from an issue with that line, the project's manifest, `.invariant/invariant.json`, records it in a new `agent` field. An amendment keeps its project's manifest as it is (D-0046), so its own line picks the agent for that issue alone, and a person moves a project to another agent by changing its manifest.
- `invariant watch` takes `-agent`, the default for everything else: `claude-code` unless it says otherwise, so projects that choose nothing stay on Claude Code. `formalize` and `synthesize`, which run the same agents by hand, take it too.
- An issue's agent is its own line's, else its project's manifest's, else the watcher's default. Every agent the factory runs for the issue is that one: the draft of its statements, its plumbing plan or its plan of issues, its build, and the second agent's review of a driver or a plumbing change (D-0087, D-0108).
- An issue that picks an agent the watcher can't run, or one it doesn't know, is answered before anything's drafted: the answer names the agents the watcher can run, the issue is labeled for a person, and nothing is drafted or built, as a plumbing issue on another repository is answered (D-0121).

What the gate checks doesn't change, and scope still refuses any change to an existing project's manifest but its code's parameters (D-0086). SPEC.md and the README say how an issue picks its agent (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Name the agent in every record of the factory's work
issues.body:
Once a project can choose its agent, every record of the factory's work says which agent did it (#153): the agent that drafted what was ratified, and the agent that built the code. Today only a pull request's synthesis or build line names it.

- Each agent run's record under `refs/invariant/runs/` names its agent from the moment it's recorded, before the run starts, and its result keeps it (D-0069, D-0073).
- The factory's posts name the agent: a draft's post, whether it asks, proposes or is stuck, names the agent that drafted it, and a build's post, passed or failed, the agent that built it. Each post's marker records the agent beside the spend it already records, and the merge post's numbers name every agent that ran for the issue (D-0062).
- A pull request's body names the agent that drafted what was ratified, the one that built it and the one that reviewed it (D-0087, D-0108).
- The receipt a factory pull request carries names the agent that built the code. CI's receipt reads only the repository, so it names the project's agent when its manifest records one. The fingerprint leaves the agent out, so a local run and CI's still match, and what the gate checks doesn't change (D-0013).
- The watcher's status file names the agent of each step it's running, for the dashboard (D-0113).

A record names the agent, `claude-code` or `codex`, and nothing else about it. SPEC.md and the README say so (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Take back only regular files from an agent's workspace
issues.body:
The factory reads what an agent leaves in its workspace, and copies some of it into the repository: a draft's proposal and model, a plumbing plan and its tests, and a build's files. Claude Code's agents have only file tools, which can't make a link (D-0037). Codex's agent, which later issues add, has a shell, and a shell can leave a link in the workspace that points at a file on the host, such as the factory's App key (D-0044). The agent can't read that file, but the factory can, so following the link would commit the file's text. This issue closes that before Codex runs (#153).

- Everywhere the factory reads or copies a file from an agent's workspace, it takes a regular file only. A symbolic link, or a hard link to a file elsewhere, is refused and never followed, and the step says which file it refused.
- A plumbing build's files come back this way too (D-0108).
- Nothing changes for a workspace that holds only regular files, as Claude Code's do today.

Tests leave a link in a workspace, pointing outside it at a file that stands in for the key, and show that no draft, plan or build takes that file's text. SPEC.md says the factory takes back only regular files (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Add a Codex backend that runs Codex headless
issues.body:
The factory's agents run through `synth.Backend`, and Claude Code is its only implementation. `synth.Codex`, named `codex`, is the second: it runs `codex exec`, Codex's documented headless mode, on @gitdek's own Codex account, and takes every job Claude Code takes, under the same rules and limits (D-0028, D-0052, #153).

- Tools: Invariant's MCP server, from the job, is Codex's only MCP server, with only the job's tools allowed, and as long for a call as Claude Code's jobs give it, since a gate run takes minutes. The run has a Codex home of its own, so nothing in the user's own Codex configuration, servers or history applies. Codex's sandbox writes only in the workspace, with no network (D-0014). A read-only job, a reviewer's, gets Codex's read-only sandbox and no server (D-0087).
- Limits: Invariant's tool caps gate and test runs, and the job's context caps its time, as now. Where Codex has no cap of its own for turns or spend, the backend keeps one from Codex's events: it stops the run at the turn cap, and at a token budget, since on an account Codex reports tokens rather than a cost. The effort D-0114 sets becomes Codex's reasoning effort, max its highest.
- What it reports: it reads Codex's JSON events into the same `synth.Usage`: the model, turns, tool calls by kind, whether Invariant's server connected, how the run ended, its last message as the summary, and its tokens. It copies every event to the job's transcript, for the live view.

Nothing runs it yet. Codex's own sandbox stops writes and the network outside its workspace, but not reads, so the factory runs Codex only once the next issue gives it a place where it can see nothing but its workspace, and settles there where its login lives (D-0037). Until then, the watcher still answers an issue that picks codex as one it can't run. Tests use a stand-in for `codex` that records its arguments and environment and replays events, since the plumbing sandbox has neither Codex nor a network. SPEC.md says the backend exists and doesn't run yet (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Run Codex where it can see nothing but its workspace
issues.body:
Codex's own sandbox stops writes and the network outside its workspace, but not reads, and the home directory holds the factory's App key (D-0044) and other credentials. So Codex can't run where Claude Code's agents do, with the home directory denied them only by Claude Code's own rules (D-0037). The factory runs it where it can see nothing but its workspace and call nothing but Invariant's tool, with no network but what Codex needs to reach its own service, and no secrets (D-0014). Then the factory runs Codex for every issue or project that picks it: drafting, planning, building and reviewing (#153).

How it does that is @gitdek's decision to ratify before it's built, so this issue's draft asks it as a fork first, with what each option costs. The options include:
- A container: an image pinned by its recipe, holding Codex's CLI, with only the workspace mounted and outbound traffic only to Codex's service. Invariant's tool stays on the host, since the gate inside the container would need Docker's socket, which reaches the home directory anyway (D-0123), so the container reaches the tool another way.
- A separate macOS user that can read nothing of @gitdek's, which the factory runs Codex as.
- macOS's own sandbox, around Codex and everything it starts.

Each answers where Codex's login lives, since whatever Codex can read, its commands can read too. The answer is recorded as a decision once this lands (D-0122).

Whatever is chosen:
- Every Codex job runs this way, and none any other way. The watcher, `formalize` and `synthesize` run Codex with the flags they have, and the ones only Codex needs, such as its model and token budget.
- Everything after the agent's run is as it is for Claude Code: the workspace, the tool, the transcript, and the files the factory takes back, which are regular files only.
- Tests check what the plumbing sandbox can: that a Codex job starts only through the isolation, with nothing but its workspace in reach. An integration test, which a person runs, shows that a job can't read a file standing in for the key.

SPEC.md and the README say where Codex runs, and that the factory runs it (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Check at start that the watcher can run its agents
issues.body:
The watcher runs whichever agent an issue or project picks, so before it takes any issue, it checks that it can run each agent it may be asked for: its `-agent` default, and every agent a project's manifest names on the base branch (#153). For each, it checks what running it needs: its CLI is installed and runs, it's logged in, and, for Codex, the place it runs in is ready. Missing any, the watcher doesn't start, and names the fix for each, such as installing Codex or running `codex login`, as it names the fix for a repository that can't merge its pull requests (D-0120).

An agent that only an issue's own line picks is still answered on that issue when the watcher can't run it.

The checks read versions and login status only: they print no credential, start no agent run and spend nothing. Tests use stand-ins for each CLI. SPEC.md and the README say what the watcher needs for each agent (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Show a Codex run in the dashboard's live view
issues.body:
The dashboard's live view shows a running step from its agent's transcript: how long it has run against its limit, its turns, tool calls, files, checks and thinking (D-0116). It reads Claude Code's events only. It reads Codex's too, so a Codex run shows as a Claude Code run does (#153).

- The watcher's status names each step's agent, and the view reads the transcript as that agent writes it.
- From Codex's events it shows the same things: the turns; each tool call in time, by kind, with Invariant's gate, check and test as now, a file change as an edit, and anything else, a shell command included, as other; the files it changed inside its copy, and those it read where Codex's events say; its tokens and context where Codex reports them; and its thinking where Codex reports reasoning, as stretches with their estimated tokens.
- Checks and time against the limit come from the step's logs and the status file, as now, whatever the agent.
- It keeps what it keeps now and nothing more: counts, times and paths inside the agent's copy, as the agent names them there. Never a command, code, the agent's words or reasoning, or the model (D-0051).
- The page names the step's agent.

Tests replay a Codex transcript and a Claude Code one through the view. SPEC.md says the live view shows either agent (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Say how to give Codex the decision graph's tools
issues.body:
A coding agent working in this repository asks the decision graph through Invariant's MCP tools, which `.mcp.json` starts for agents that read that file (D-0106). Codex doesn't read it. It reads MCP servers from its own configuration, `~/.codex/config.toml`, which `codex mcp add` writes. AGENTS.md and the README say how to give Codex the same server, `invariant mcp -decisions -write` for the checkout, so a person working here with Codex has the same tools (#153).

- The docs give the Codex configuration to copy, and say how it finds the checkout: started in it, or named with `-C`.
- A test reads `.mcp.json` and the Codex configuration in the docs, and fails when the docs' configuration doesn't start the server `.mcp.json` starts, so the two can't drift apart.

AGENTS.md is in the trusted base, so a person merges this. SPEC.md says Codex gets the tools from its own configuration (D-0122).

Kind: plumbing

usage.summary: I've written `issues.json` with eight plumbing issues, and it passed the check on the first try: first how an issue or project chooses Codex or Claude Code (with Claude Code the default) and a record of which agent did each piece of work, then Codex itself, then its start check, live view and docs. I didn't write `proposal.json`: how Codex is kept to its workspace is the one choice that changes the build, and I left it as a question for @gitdek on the fifth issue, to answer before anything is built, rather than holding up the whole plan for it.
